scheme: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH from 1.0.0. +1.0.0 for a bulk/architectural change, +0.1.0 for a system change, +0.0.1 for an image set. Components never wrap — 1.0.99 goes to 1.0.100.

major.baseline: 1.0.0 — 2026-07-17, the public gallery launched. MAJOR 1 is where the scheme starts, not a bump, which is why `counted` holds five items across four bumps.
counted: MAJOR 2 — 2026-07-30 — the measured pipeline rebuild: ~30 operations down to 8, every stage measured, 14 findings recorded in PIPELINE_PRINCIPLES.md
MAJOR 3 — 2026-07-31 — the sky dome: the album mapped onto the celestial sphere, with a measured coverage figure

MAJOR 3 — 2026-08-01/04 — per-class presets, the --class QC harness, and M 31-anchored per-target recipes. Landed inside the same bump as the sky dome rather than a second one — changelog era 3, "The sky dome, and conditioning per target", is named for both

MAJOR 4 — 2026-08-04 — the gallery restructure: one card per target instead of one per photo, four viewing modes behind it (raw stack, integration showcase, conditioned, before/after), split-colour card borders, sky-dome search and reference circles. The grid stopped being a list of files and became a list of subjects, which is a change of shape rather than of degree

MAJOR 5 — 2026-08-20 — the murk rebuild: the whole album re-rendered from its original exposures on a changed stack. Combining now skips the colour-mosaic interpolation that was clumping the noise before processing began (CFA drizzle, pixfrac 0.7; sky noise correlation 0.23 at the sensor vs 0.68 after the old combine), the finisher smooths less and treats the 4-64 px band it had never measured, and the registration reference is pinned per target so framing cannot drift. 31 conditioned renders replaced; the mid/fine noise balance improved on all 31 and three crushed-shadow faults (M 63, NGC 6742, NGC 6946) went with it. Ledger: siril/testing/MURK.md

MAJOR 6 — 2026-08-21 — the album made small and navigable. What a cold visitor downloads before anything paints went 3.18 MB to 0.74 MB, and a full grid scroll 30.8 MB to 1.08 MB, by giving the grid its own 400px thumbnail tier and trimming data/openngc.json from 10,016 catalogue entries to the 557 this album can reach. Cards gained a count badge and a stable per-image number, the grid gained ten collapsing type sections with filters and debounced search, and the viewer gained a slideshow and per-viewer starring. Architectural rather than cosmetic: the grid is now a pure gridRenderPlan() the DOM merely renders, and its card count is bounded by (sections x page) rather than by album size — measured at 213 cards for 2,000 subjects.

MAJOR 7 — 2026-09-20 — the album explains itself, and can be written back to. Someone who had never seen the site was watched using it: they landed on the hero, scrolled a little, and never reached the large viewer at all. Seventeen changes came out of that. The page now walks a visitor to the picture (a scroll of its own, a card that draws an arrow to each of the four viewing modes, a slideshow on by default that opens with the album's strongest work), and 'strongest' is measured rather than remembered — tools/score_clarity.py scores every published photograph on star density, extended structure and noise, which took four corrections to get honest (a lunar stack reporting 62,000 stars per megapixel, a solar disc whose median IS the disc, a Venus crescent dividing by a near-zero dynamic range, and an unbounded structure term that put three solar-system frames at a perfect 100). The viewer was rebuilt around the photograph: information directly under it, controls on the arrows' row, the single-letter (i)/(n)/(s) discs gone, a labelled Close up backed by 75 crops cut at 1:1 from the album's own full-size photographs, a Wikipedia link, and a full-screen view that follows the slideshow and turns a portrait frame to fill a landscape screen. Planets mark themselves with a crosshair — and can, now that a hand-placed callout no longer needs a plate solve to be drawn, which is why Pluto's marker had never once appeared. And the site gained a voice back: one Cloudflare Worker (public_gallery/site_worker/) serving the wishlist that had never been switched on, a feedback box whose recipient and subject are constants so there is nothing for an injected header to inject into, and the visitor counts THE APP now reads back in its own System drawer. 26 adversarial checks against that Worker, and the gallery harness — which had silently been skipping every check after its boot test — restored and extended.
major.eras: public_gallery/changelog.json declares one era per MAJOR above, and every entry there points at the era it belongs to. tools/deposit_check.py FAILS if the highest era declared is not MAJOR here. Eras 4 and 5 were missing for sixteen days before that check existed: the panel stamped v5.31.32 at its head while its newest band still read v3.

minor.50_to_52: Set alongside the version string rather than incremented blind: `count` read 50 while `version` read 51, the same drift PATCH had. The +1 is the 2026-08-26 mosaic re-solve, which changed what the dome draws, and the sky-dome brightness control shipped with it.
minor.means: system change that is not a bulk rewrite
minor.counted: 6 public site changes recorded as `website` in the changelog, plus 18 internal system changes evidenced in git — Windows migration, Start Album launcher, master dark build + wiring, protected-chain --finish/preset plumbing, qc_report --class, DESIGN_INTENTS H/N/K, target_recipe anchoring, integration showcase, midnight-session new-badge fix, mosaic coverage mask, the pipeline notice, PWA photo_options ledger, plate-solve cache, rescan EXIF carry-forward, serve.py port-walk + truststore, gitignore/launcher work, showcase alignment, showcase colour calibration, the stale-render check (a sub captured after its master was built cannot be in it), the detached-preview fix in run_watched, the Eagle/Omega showcase rebuilt to its full 4 h 33 m, and the family note cut from three sentences to one, the Eagle-and-Omega field gathered from two stash folders the Seestar named separately and restacked to 7 h 28 m, its showcase earning a five-hour step, 39 renders reshipped, the Condition button taught to stage and restack a night instead of re-conditioning yesterday's master, and SPCC moved off the network onto the full 20.8 GB local catalogue, the Eagle and Omega taken to 10 h 01 m over five nights and the Cygnus Loop to 2 h 19 m, both restacked on their pinned framing; the Veil's showcase rebuilt to six rungs and its before/after repaired after comparing two pointings 46 deg apart
added_since_3_22: 2026-08-04 — the changelog panel became a version timeline: collapsible major-version eras, bulleted entries, the album version stamped at its head (`website`)
2026-08-04 — the integration showcase gained a frozen PCC colour calibration, its promotion bar became ladder rungs rather than hours, and NGC 6960 was built (internal)

2026-08-18 — the deposit path became repeatable and the cross-machine ledger was repaired: /deposit-from-telescope encodes the whole night-to-published run, and data/photo_options.json was backfilled after 13 albumed objects were found missing from it. That ledger is the only thing suppressing Tonight's Best, so those 13 were still being recommended on the other machine — it demonstrably cost four re-shoots (NGC 188, NGC 6791, NGC 6866, NGC 7261). sync_manifest.py also produced its first Windows manifest, so the Mac can finally see Windows-side photos (internal)

2026-08-18 — the sky dome's two faults and their causes: stack previews now colour-calibrate before export (four frames were shipping with the full light-pollution cast, R/B 2.48 against 1.01), and plate solves are validated against the file they describe so a replaced image cannot be drawn through the previous frame's geometry (`website`)

2026-08-18 — the album detects where it is and how dark the sky is there: a stored location is re-checked against IP geolocation on load and a move is OFFERED rather than applied, and Bortle now comes from a bundled VIIRS-derived atlas (15 classes, sampled server-side, works with no signal) instead of a dropdown defaulted to 5 (internal)

2026-08-18 — the published gallery gained a tab icon (the North America Nebula, matching the app and launcher). publish.py ships icons/ and warns if one is missing rather than silently falling back to the browser glyph (`website`)

2026-08-19 — the frozen stretch curve is anchored to the data it is applied to. --curve-from froze both the WIDTH and the POSITION of the curve on the pre-denoise frame; GraXpert shifts the level by up to 3x on some targets, so the shadow clip sat above 99.5% of the pixels and four renders (NGC 654, NGC 6712, NGC 6946, NGC 891 — two of them clusters) came out 99% pure black. H1 divided by the resulting zero sky noise and PASSED them at 2.3e7, which is why nothing reported it; new H0 gates that. All four rebuilt from the same exposures (`website`)

2026-08-19 — the compare-slider rotation wedge is cropped out of both pair members. Aligning the raw onto the conditioned frame rotates it, which leaves empty corners; invisible while the raw only lived under the slider, visible once RAW STACK became a mode of its own. Five pairs were affected (IC 1848, M 20, M 31, M 81, NGC 6791) with NGC 6791 and M 20 worst at 2.1% and 2.0% of frame black. Both members take the SAME symmetric inset so the pair stays registered to the pixel; every warped member measures 0.000% black afterwards, at a cost of 2.5-9% of frame area and 23% on the most-rotated pair (`website`)

2026-08-20 — a stack preview is placed by the pair it belongs to, not by the clock. The preview is the compare slider's 'before'; publish pairs either by a declared pair in photo_options.json or by matching date, and the preview used time.strftime() for its filename. Conditioning that finishes after midnight — routine, since the session itself crosses midnight — then dated the preview a day later than its render, so it matched neither rule and the slider silently fell back to the Seestar's single-night JPG. NGC 6822's 70-sub preview shipped as 2026-08-20 beside a 2026-08-19 render. pipelines._preview_dst() now resolves the exact slot and the run prints 'replaced', which is the tell that it landed (internal)

2026-08-21 — the sky dome stopped letting an unfinished mosaic mask its neighbours. Frames were averaged by FOOTPRINT overlap, so a mosaic's unimaged area both painted black over the graticule and divided every frame beneath it (6% of covered points inside Sadr's footprint, worst at 50% brightness). Both now key off whether a frame actually holds light there. Also: plate solving gained the mount's own pointing as its hint and an undecimated retry, taking the unsolvable set from 10 to 4 (`website`)

2026-08-21 — three faults the album could not show you it had. A download button was wired from the slide's item before the mode branches replaced the picture, so in showcase mode it handed over the raw stack instead of the milestone on screen; all button writing now goes through one function and every label carries the word Download. The sky dome averaged overlapping frames by coverage alone, so a 39.7 min Lagoon stack and a 12.5 min Trifid stack at the same centre contributed half each and the deep one read as absent — overlaps are now weighted by integration time (data/frame_depth.json), giving it 85% of its overlap and the M 24 mosaic 95% over the 9-sub tile it supersedes. The integration showcase cross-fades between milestones instead of cutting, and says which two stacks it is between rather than naming a figure the blend does not represent (`website`)

2026-08-21 — custom capture: draw a rectangle on the sky dome and every photograph inside it is composited into one image, which lands on the main screen with a download button. The region is defined on the sky (centre, basis, half-angles) rather than on the screen, so it survives panning, and its roll is frozen when drawn — read live it spun the region about its centre whenever the viewer looked elsewhere. Rendering reuses the dome's own footprintPass, so a capture inherits the data-aware coverage, the integration-depth weighting and the divide-once composite instead of drifting from the map it was taken from; plate edges are feathered and the uncovered outer margin is cropped. Verified under headless SwiftShader at 2 frames/1079x909 and 9 frames/3179x2189, which is what caught the capture asking only for detail tiers and rendering placeholder plates. A brightness stretch was tried and rejected — the dome's tiles are hard JPEG and 10x of gain surfaced their 8x8 blocks (`website`)

2026-08-21 — custom capture, reworked after use. Two points cannot describe a rectangle on the sky (five degrees of freedom, four numbers), and every assumption that closed the gap was a fault: square to the screen meant it would not rotate, and preferring landscape swapped the extents so a vertical selection stopped containing its own points. Three handles now — one edge sets rotation and width, the third sets height. Sharpness stopped depending on the zoom: refine() hands back any texture finer than the current view needs, so the tiers a capture had just fetched were released again a moment later, and two captures of the same sky came out with high-frequency detail of 5.40 and 0.36; the same region captured from 60 degrees and from close in is now byte-identical. Overlap weights are proportional to integration time, which is the inverse-variance combination stacking itself uses — 1.5 had been chosen to make a deep frame win and overcorrected. Also: the mirror in the region basis (u = c x r rather than r x c), the full-resolution preview, and a (?) that plays a screen recording of the tool in use (`website`)
2026-08-21 — tools/reclaim_disk.py. Frees only what it can PROVE is redundant, file by file, against the archive; 107.8 GB reclaimed with both copies intact.
2026-08-21 — tools/mirror_archive.py. Copies the 88.74 GB that has no offsite copy and hash-verifies it. Never deletes at the destination.
2026-08-21 — tools/check_live_downloads.py. HEADs all 209 download targets on the DEPLOYED site — the only layer that can catch a case-only filename difference, which Windows cannot reproduce.

2026-08-21 — the viewer, reworked around what a reader is actually looking at. A target opens on its deepest photograph and the card previews the same one, so the integration figure printed on a card finally describes the picture above it (4 covers changed). Targets with several photographs show them as a filmstrip rather than a 2/3 stepper that never said what the others were. The prev/next arrows moved onto the picture, the slideshow walks a shuffled order, and the slide cross-fades between photographs. Two miscategorised targets: IC 1318 was filed under Stars because OpenNGC resolves that id to gam Cyg — Sadr, the star in front of the nebula — and the merge took the star's type; the catalogue now wins whenever OpenNGC disagrees about the KIND of object, audited across all 95 catalogued targets. The Sun moved to Solar System, where the section is named for it. The sky dome's frames now arrive from random points on the sphere over three seconds, its zoom scale stopped running off the edge of the window, and its capture help stopped covering the Snap shot button (`website`)

2026-08-22 — MINOR 39→40: the Lagoon/Trifid mix-up and two download faults, plus a composition guide on the capture rectangle and a Goto Sky Dome button on the slide. The photograph titled Lagoon Nebula had the Trifid dead centre and the Lagoon clipped against the left edge; the two frames were swapped by filename, which is the album's only object-assignment mechanism, and every path-keyed cache rekeyed with them so nothing needed re-solving. Every one of the 155 plate-solved photographs was then audited against data/frame_contents.json for the same fault; the Lagoon was the only frame whose target was clipped by the edge while another catalogued object sat at the centre (`website`) The slide button flies the dome to the FRAME rather than the target — M 31 has four photographs at three pointings — and is hidden on the 19 photographs with no plate solve, since opening the dome and not moving is a worse answer than not offering. tools/check_labels.py is the audit, kept as a tool: it passes on the corrected data and, fed the state that shipped, reports the two Lagoon files and nothing else.

2026-08-23 — MINOR 40→41: publish's deploy preflight is machine-aware. rescan.py began unioning album_inventory.json the same day so an incomplete photos/ could not gut the ledger, but preflight compares that union against THIS machine's photos/ — so the five images that live only on the Mac (M 20 2026-07-14 raw and conditioned, M 31 2026-06-30, M 81 2026-07-23, NGC 7023 2026-07-26) read as deletions and refused the deploy. Two changes that each individually hold up: together they meant no deposit from Windows could publish, and the Mac would have been refused over the 116 Windows-only images in turn. Preflight now excuses a missing file that another machine's .sync manifest claims, and still fails on one no machine claims — verified both ways before shipping. Its own manifest cannot excuse its own gap (internal)

2026-08-23 — MINOR 41→42: three faults on the sky dome, each measured before it was fixed. (1) Frames were flattened for BRIGHTNESS only — one luminance surface fitted and subtracted from R, G and B alike, which by construction cannot remove a gradient that is warm at one end and cool at the other. 83 of 144 tiles carried one; NGC 6625 showed it as an orange wedge. Flattening is now per channel where it is needed, gated at a colour spread of 0.016 — swept over all 188 solved frames and chosen by 90th-percentile residual, which is flat from 0.012 to 0.018: p90 0.0456→0.0193, worst frame 0.1471→0.0592, and zero regressions among frames that reach the dome. (2) The texture ladder was a fixed pixel count, so a 7.8 deg mosaic got 262 px/deg against an ordinary frame's 554 and discarded 3.75x of its own resolution — that, not geometry, is why mosaics looked smeared. Tiers now follow angular size; 4 frames qualify, ~5 MB fetched on demand, first paint untouched. (3) A mosaic is nine tangent planes stitched together and one linear WCS cannot describe it: M 24's stars drifted from 8.1 arcsec at its centre to 15.2 at 3 deg out (+1.55 arcsec/deg) while Sadr's stayed flat, which is why the correction is FITTED per frame rather than assumed for mosaics. tools/fit_dome_distortion.py fits a second-order-only term against the consensus of every other frame that sees the same star; constant and linear terms are discarded so the plate solve keeps sole authority over position, rotation and scale and the fit can only bend a frame. It is applied at the mesh vertices, so no texture is resampled. 2 of 190 frames qualified; M 24's outer residual halved to 7.5 arcsec and its slope went +1.55 to -0.32 arcsec/deg. Earlier threshold settings kept 19 and then 22 frames — most winning 0.1-0.6 arcsec on frames already at the ~2 arcsec solve-to-solve floor, which is fitting noise onto published astrometry — and one clustered fit wanted to move V1331 Aquilae's far edge by 129 arcsec. The spread and meaningful-gain guards were calibrated against those specific failures (internal + `website`)

2026-08-23 — MINOR 42→43: the dome fixes, done properly, after the first attempt was measured against the wrong quantity and shipped a regression. (a) The 6.42.35 deploy DROPPED the album's four widest mosaics: the per-frame tier ladder wrote to build/sky/4096/, which the mkdir loop never created because it ran once from the default ladder. Coverage fell 977.1 to 910.7 deg^2 and publish still exited 0 and force-pushed. Preflight now treats a solved frame failing to build as fatal, with no --allow- flag. (b) The grey rectangles were never a colour fault. flatten_for_dome fitted its surface to the darkest 65% of pixels, which on a gradient is not a sample of the background but a sample of its DARK END — the mask is spatially biased, the surface follows it, the bright side stays uncorrected. Sigma clipping instead (fit all, drop what sits above, refit; asymmetric so a rotated frame's empty corners cannot drag it down) takes the residual luminance spread from 0.0209 to 0.0039 median on the shipped textures, and colour 0.0118 to 0.0039. The per-channel gate added at 6.42.35 is gone: it only existed to contain the damage the biased mask did. (c) The star smearing was two frames drawn a few pixels apart, not blur. V1331 Aquilae's plate solve sits 13.6 arcsec off three independently solved neighbours, which all agree on the direction; re-solving undecimated, tight and auto-scale returns the same centre to under 4 arcsec, because a nine-tile stitch has no exact single-tangent-plane solution. The correction model therefore gained a TRANSLATION term, gated not on a magnitude cap but on two or more independently solved neighbours agreeing — and fitted as a constant-only model, because reading the constant off a six-term fit of clustered matches returns the polynomial extrapolated to a plate centre no star constrains, which asked for an 85 arcsec correction to a 13.6 arcsec error. Rotation and scale are still never touched. In the region the smear was reported, V1331's disagreement with its neighbours went 13.8/16.1/16.3 to 5.8/7.1/9.7 arcsec. 30 frames corrected, 25 curvature-only, 4 shift+curvature, 1 shift-only. (d) Captures now carry the exact region and their contributing frame list in a JPEG comment, read by tools/read_capture.py — which is how (c) was diagnosed at all (internal + `website`)

2026-08-23 - MINOR 43->44: a deploy must be looked at before it goes out. publish.py --deploy no longer builds; it publishes the tree that --preview served and --approve fingerprinted, byte for byte, and refuses if the fingerprint has moved or the approval is over six hours old. There is deliberately no flag to skip it. The reason is a fault earlier the same day: a per-frame texture tier wrote into a directory nothing had created, the album's four widest mosaics failed to build, and publish printed '!! 4 SOLVED frame(s) failed to build and are MISSING from the map', exited 0 and force-pushed. Coverage fell 977.1 to 910.7 deg^2 and the site was wrong for an hour. Every automated check in the deposit workflow passed on that build, because none of them look at the pictures - and a rebuild-then-push deploy can always ship pixels nobody saw. Preflight separately gained a hard refusal on any solved frame that fails to build, since unlike a removal or a dirty tree there is no intended version of that. Verified four ways before shipping: no approval refuses, a matching approval passes, a ONE-BYTE change to build/ refuses, and a nine-hour-old approval refuses (internal)

2026-08-23 - MINOR 44->45: the two dome faults, fixed, after the first attempt at each was measured against the wrong thing. (a) SMEARED STARS were not astrometry and not the mesh - they were resampling. Every frame was served at about 54% of the sensor's own sampling (524-554 px/deg against 983), and that halving is what turned round stars into ellipses: measured star ellipticity 0.596 at the old top tier against 0.376 in the native data. Tiers now target the sensor's sampling, and the shipped textures measure 0.392/0.391/0.461/0.444 for V1331, M 24, M 11 and NGC 6683 - at or below each frame's own data floor. It costs 195 MB of on-demand texture; first paint is unchanged at 0.81 MB. (b) The ASTROMETRY tool was rewritten because it had been making frames worse. It used the album as its reference, and nearest-neighbour star matching overstates disagreement in a dense field - every detection finds SOMETHING inside the match radius. V1331 Aquilae's 22013 detections gave a 13.55 arcsec disagreement; measured against a catalogue it is 3.90. The tool corrected a 3.9 arcsec error by 13 and shipped the frame at 6.30. It now cuts each frame into tiles small enough for one tangent plane and lets ASTAP solve them against its own catalogue - an external reference over the whole plate, no cross-matching. 172 of 190 frames turn out to be within 2.5 arcsec already and are left alone; 5 are corrected, all verified on held-out references. (c) The ORANGE CORNER was cloud in V430 Scuti, and four hand-built detectors failed to tell it from nebulosity before GraXpert did it in one pass: 83% of V430's large-scale excess removed against 7% off the Trifid, whose nebula came out stronger. Every dome texture is now background-extracted; V430 went 0.1565 to 0.0246, level with its neighbours, while the Trifid, Andromeda and the Eagle keep theirs. Coverage and the star count are re-anchored to the ORIGINAL frames so a display decision cannot move a published measurement - 977.1 deg^2 before and after (internal + `website`)

2026-08-23 - MINOR 45->46: three faults reported against the 6.45 preview, none of which had reached the live site. (a) FLICKER when zoomed in was VRAM thrashing introduced by the native-sampling tiers: the budget was 160 MB, but a 4096 texture is 33.6 MB and an 8192 one is 134.2 MB, so two neighbouring frames at their top tier evicted each other every refine and 'sharpening...' never cleared. 512 MB. (b) The LIGHTER MOSAIC was two faults stacked. GraXpert fills in a mosaic's unimaged wedges - M 24 went 23.7% black to 2.0% - and those invented pixels then counted as valid sky in the flatten, lifting the whole frame and painting over its neighbours; the original's black mask is re-applied exactly. Under that sat the real one, which Nathan diagnosed: DOME_SKY assumes the darkest sky in a frame means the same brightness everywhere, and in M 24 the sigma-clipped fit anchors to the dark nebulae B92 and B93, so its ORDINARY sky lands above everyone else's. tools/fit_dome_levels.py solves per-frame per-channel offsets making overlapping frames agree where they overlap - a least squares over the overlap graph, mean pinned to zero. M 24 went 0.0654 to 0.0614 to 0.0588, into the middle of its neighbours; measured independently on the shipped textures the step across a seam went median 0.00312 to 0.00241, p90 0.00965 to 0.00661. (c) BENT EDGES were a model too stiff to follow them. Beyond 0.45 of the half-diagonal, against ASTAP's catalogue: V1331 10.67 arcsec uncorrected, 2.98 at order 2, 0.79 at order 3; NGC 7000 5.29/1.27/0.19; Sadr 8.53/4.49/1.71; M 24 3.66/1.87/0.31. Order 3 now, the shape a SIP solution uses. V1331's outer bin 12.57 to 0.68 arcsec, its whole plate 3.81 to 0.61, held-out falling with it. The earlier refusal to fit constant and linear terms was right when the reference was the ALBUM and wrong once it became a catalogue. 12 frames corrected, up from 5 (internal + `website`)

2026-08-23 - MINOR 46->47: the bright rim along an unfinished mosaic's tile edges. GraXpert cannot tell 'not photographed' from 'very dark sky', so the black wedges dragged its background model toward them and it under-subtracted nearby, leaving the frame brightest along every tile boundary. M 24's ORIGINAL is flat to a percent across the whole plate - median brightness at 4-40 / 100-200 / 400-800 / 1600+ source pixels from a wedge reads 0.1438 / 0.1451 / 0.1451 / 0.1477 - while the extraction of it read 0.1634 / 0.1399 / 0.1242 / 0.1150. The unimaged area is now filled with the frame's own local sky BEFORE extraction and the original mask reinstated exactly afterwards, so nothing invented is published. Edge-to-centre ratio, where 1.000 is no rim: M 24 1.47 -> 0.94, V1331 Aquilae 1.75 -> 1.06. 184 frames re-extracted and the levels re-solved against them (pairwise disagreement 0.00299 -> 0.00028). Recorded because it cost a wrong diagnosis first: the rim was assumed to be Lanczos ringing off the hard mask, and only a direct test disproved it - the profile was IDENTICAL with a hard zero, with a smooth fill, and with a BOX filter, which rules out resampling entirely. The extend-before-resize code from that detour is kept: it is harmless and does prevent ringing, but it was not the bug. Remaining: some frames now read slightly DARK at the edge instead (NGC 7000 at 0.67-0.77), which may be real tile vignetting (internal + `website`)

2026-08-23 - MINOR 47->48: sky-dome textures carry a content hash in their URL. They were the only published asset that did not: index.html has referenced gallery.js and gallery.css as `?v=<hash>` for months, but a dome texture lived at a stable path, so when its pixels changed the URL did not. GitHub Pages serves them with Cache-Control: max-age=600, which is long enough that a deploy reads as not having happened - reported immediately after 6.47.35 as 'how come I still see the triangle edge after updating?', when the bytes on the server were already byte-identical to the approved build. Verified that way rather than guessed: the live JPEGs were fetched and md5-compared against the local build before anything was changed. A changed texture is now a different URL and no cache can answer for it (internal + `website`)

2026-08-25 — MINOR 48->49: the new-arrivals band became the CALENDAR WEEK (Mon-Sun) containing the newest drop, replacing a rolling seven days back from it. The rolling window moved every night, so an object's badge expired on whatever weekday it happened to be shot and "new" never had a meaning a visitor could read off the page; a week graduates at once instead. tools/deposit_check.py had imported NEW_ARRIVAL_DAYS and then re-implemented the window around it — which was enough while the shape was "count back N days" and would have silently disagreed here, since the constant is still 7 either way. It now imports publish.drop_dates_for(), so the shape cannot drift either. Also: config.ASTAP prefers astap_cli, the console build — the windowed astap.exe raises a window and STEALS KEYBOARD FOCUS once per solve, which makes the machine unusable across a hundreds-of-frames pass. That exposed a second fault: astap_cli does not write the DIMENSIONS key, so parse_ini fell through to image_size [0,0] on all 10 new frames — the exact field the stale-solve guard compares against the file, so deposit_check reported them all stale. It now reads the size from the FILE, which is the authority ASTAP was only echoing. NGC 6383 added to the hand-curated catalog.json; it is absent from the OpenNGC extract, which jumps 6382 to 6384 (internal + `website`)

2026-08-25 — MINOR 49->50: 38 album targets had no card in the published grid. scrub_openngc trims the shipped catalogue to objects inside a solved frame's circumscribed circle plus catalog.json, and it built the object's unit vector with math.radians(o['ra']) — but RA in these catalogues is decimal HOURS while the cones are built from crval in DEGREES. Every object landed at a fifteenth of its true RA, the cone test essentially never fired, and the trim kept little more than catalog.json (555 of 10016). gallery.js buildItems() resolves a photo's object with `CATALOG.objects.find(o => o.id === objId)` and drops the photo on a miss, so any album target living only in OpenNGC — NGC 6229, NGC 6781, IC 4604, IC 4605, NGC 6568 and 33 others — was silently absent from the grid. Fixed to ra * 15: kept goes 555 -> 589 and album objects unresolvable by the gallery go 41 -> 0. Nothing caught it because rescan.py resolves against the FULL OpenNGC, so the data layer was consistent with itself and every deposit check passed. The client had it right all along (gallery.js:1984, `obj.ra * 15`) (`website`)

On a 14.2 x 4.5 deg capture of Sagittarius it was the M 24 mosaic: 256 px over 7.8 deg is 33 px/deg against the 498 px/deg the output asked for, and its depth weight was the heaviest for two degrees around, so the blend went to the blurred copy. Nothing reported it and every check passed — the fault was visible only in the picture, and provable only from the capture's own embedded frame list, which recorded 21 frames at the right tier and simply did not mention the 22nd. Fixed with a separating-axis test on the two convex quads projected into the region's tangent plane, the third case the function's own comment had described but never implemented; the two lists are now one, so the set that is drawn is the set that is prepared and the set that is reported. minor.58_to_59: The Lagoon's conditioned render stopped being one tone curve. TWO complete renders are made, midtone 0.42 and 0.70, and core_blend.py interpolates between them per pixel on a sigmoid of the blurred luminance (sigma 120, k 3). 0.70 holds gradation in the core, 0.42 keeps the faint outer cloud; the mask takes whichever each region needs, so neither endpoint's failure can reach the frame. Judged against a 32-inch reference frame of the core. The mask is deliberately soft: 98.4% of pixels are a genuine mix, 1.65% reach pure bright, NONE reach pure faint, and the steepest gradient anywhere is 0.047/px — earlier hard-edged masks read as blobs with visible borders. Three attempts preceded it and qc_report caught all three, not the eye: a highlight expansion that compressed against the 1.0 ceiling (A2 0.0560 -> 0.0151), the same fix moved to the starless layer where it saturated stars (D2 28-54 px against a <12 budget), and a mid-pipeline midtone split that is now REMOVED. minor.59_to_60: tools/mosaic_patch.py: a Seestar mosaic is stitched on-device, so a sub that caught a branch is baked into the export and cannot be dropped by re-stacking. But a mosaic revisits its tiles, and an obstruction that rises into the field late was usually imaged cleanly earlier. The tool scores every sub for LARGE non-stellar bright area (stars are a few px, a branch is hundreds), masks what survived into the export, solves the damaged region and the clean subs independently, reprojects them onto the mosaic's own grid, phase-correlates the result against the mosaic to kill the residual between two solves, quantile-matches tone on the surrounding annulus and feathers in. On FLD1801S270: 5 of 117 subs obstructed (blob 1.33-7.19% against a worst-clean 0.002%), 11 clean subs covered 100% of the damage, alignment refined to 0.85 x 1.30 px, green excess in the repaired area 16.5 -> 0.4, and the region re-solves to the same sky within 0.2 arcsec. Every replaced pixel is real signal from the same night; nothing is inpainted. siril/detect_tree_frames.py does NOT cover this case and was measured doing so: it scores trees by CORNER DARKNESS and kept all 117 subs, the obstructed ones at 2.9-3.9% against its 25% threshold, because these leaves were LIT and entered mid-edge rather than filling a corner. minor.60_to_61: mosaic_patch's contamination mask tested GREENNESS, `G - max(R,B)`, and that was the wrong measurement. The first repair shipped with that flake still in the frame, and the tool's own verification agreed with itself: it reported 'green excess 16.5 -> 0.4' because it re-measured with the same blind test that made the mask. Reported by eye, not by any check. Now the test is WARMTH, `(R+G)/2 - B`: 47 on the green core, 22 on the orange flake, 0.2-2.3 on sky, and 1.5 on the Milky Way dust lane running through the same field, so real nebulosity is not touched. Masked area 0.775% -> 1.057%, 9 clean subs still covering 100% of it, and max warm excess over the whole frame 92.5 (original) -> 39.4 (first repair) -> 13.6 (now), the remainder being five compact orange STARS confirmed by eye. minor.61_to_62: Three sky-dome changes and one new instrument path.
